1.note: Jeremiah is using **the declaration of Yahweh** to indicate that what has been said is a direct quotation from Yahweh and comes with Yahweh’s authority. In your translation, use a natural way of indicating direct quotations in your language.

The pronoun **they** refers to the enemies whom Yahweh will bring against Judah, whom he does not name here. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [Judah’s enemies will bring out the bones of the kings of Judah]

2.note: Yahweh is speaking as if the stars were a **host**, that is, an army drawn up in the sky. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and to all of the many stars that fill the sky]

The pronoun **they** refers to the dead people whose bones will be spread out, not to the enemies who bring the bones out of the graves. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [which those dead people loved and which those dead people served]

Yahweh is speaking as if worshiping these heavenly bodies were traveling behind them, since he says that the people **walked after** them. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and that they followed as their gods]

The expressions **They will not be gathered** and **they will not be buried** are passive verbal forms. If it would be unnatural to use those forms, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [No one will gather them, and no one will bury them]

Yahweh is speaking as if the unburied bones were **dung**, something repugnant and worthless that is left lying on the ground. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [They will lie discarded and worthless on the surface of the ground]

4.note: This could mean: (1) Yahweh is telling Jeremiah what to say, so **I** refers to Jeremiah or (2) Yahweh is speaking about himself, so **I** refers to Yahweh. In either case, the pronoun **them** refers to the people of Judah and Jerusalem. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [And I will say to the people of Judah and Jerusalem]
If it would be clearer in your language, you could translate this so that there is not a quotation within a quotation. Alternate translation: [And I will them that Yahweh says]

Yahweh is using the question form to appeal to what everyone knows, that people who fall down get up again. If a speaker of your language would not use the question form for that purpose, you could translate this as a statement or as an exclamation. Alternate translation: [Certainly those who fall down will get up again!]

Yahweh is using the question form to appeal to what everyone knows, that a person who wanders off the road turns around and finds his way again. If a speaker of your language would not use the question form for that purpose, you could translate this as a statement or as an exclamation. Alternate translation: [If one turns away, then he certainly does return!]

5.q: מַדּ֨וּעַ שׁוֹבְבָ֜ה הָ⁠עָ֥ם הַ⁠זֶּ֛ה יְרוּשָׁלִַ֖ם מְשֻׁבָ֣ה נִצַּ֑חַת
5.note: Yahweh is using the question form to rebuke the people of Jerusalem for continuing to turn away from him when it would be natural for them to return. If a speaker of your language would not use the question form for that purpose, you could translate this as a statement or as an exclamation. Alternate translation: [This people, Jerusalem, has turned away in continuous apostasy!]

In this verse, the word **people** is singular in form, but it refers to all of the inhabitants of Jerusalem as a group. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use the plural form of “people.” Alternate translation: [Why then have these people of Jerusalem turned away]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **apostasy**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [continually turning away from me]

Yahweh is speaking as if **deceit** were an object that the people could take hold of and keep in their hands. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [They firmly commit themselves to what is false]

Yahweh is speaking as if the Israelites, who had been walking behind him but then went away in a different direction, **refuse to turn** around and walk behind him again. He means that they refuse to start living in the manner in which God wants people to live. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and refuse to start living the way I want them to live]

6.note: The terms **paid attention** and **listened** mean similar things. Yahweh is using the two terms together for emphasis. If it would be clearer for your readers, you could express the emphasis with a single phrase. Alternate translation: [I listened very carefully]

Here the masculine term **man** has a generic sense that includes both men and women. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could use language in your translation that is clearly inclusive of both men and women. Alternate translation: [There was not a person regretting over his or her wickedness]

Yahweh is speaking as if the way these people live were a set of **courses** or paths that they were running along. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [All of them return to their own way of living]

The point of this comparison is that just as **a stallion plunging into the battle** rushes ahead without any thought of the danger, so these people rush ahead in their wickedness without any thought of the consequences. If it would be helpful in your language, you could make this point explicitly. Alternate translation: [rushing ahead heedlessly, just as a stallion plunges into battle without regard for the danger]

7.note: Yahweh is not referring to a specific **stork**. He means storks in general. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could use an expression that would be more natural in your language. Alternate translation: [Even every stork in the heavens knows its appointed times]

The **turtledove**, the **swift one**, and the **crane** are kinds of birds that migrate, that is, they fly to another region and back again at the same time each year. If your readers would not be familiar with what these birds are, you could use the names of similar birds that your readers would recognize, or you could use a more general term. Alternate translation: [and other kinds of birds that migrate]

The implication is that these birds return to the land at the same season every year. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [return to this land at the same season every year]

8.q: אֵיכָ֤ה תֹֽאמְרוּ֙ חֲכָמִ֣ים אֲנַ֔חְנוּ וְ⁠תוֹרַ֥ת יְהוָ֖ה אִתָּ֑⁠נוּ
8.note: Yahweh is using the question form to deny that these people can rightly claim to be wise. If a speaker of your language would not use the question form for that purpose, you could translate this as a statement or as an exclamation. Alternate translation: [You must not say, “We are wise, and the law of Yahweh is with us.”]

8.q: אֵיכָ֤ה תֹֽאמְרוּ֙ חֲכָמִ֣ים אֲנַ֔חְנוּ וְ⁠תוֹרַ֥ת יְהוָ֖ה אִתָּ֑⁠נוּ
8.note: If it would be clearer in your language, you could translate this so that there is not a quotation within a quotation. Alternate translation: [How can you say that you are wise and that the law of Yahweh is with you?]

Here, **The stylus** represents what the scribes write with the stylus. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [The writing of the deceitful scribes]

9.note: The expressions **will be put to shame**, **will be dismayed**, and **will be captured** are passive verbal forms. If it would be unnatural to use those forms, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [will experience shame; they will feel dismay and their enemies will capture them]

Here, **the word of Yahweh** represents the message that Yahweh spoke. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [the message that Yahweh spoke]

Yahweh is using the question form to assert that these people have no wisdom at all. If a speaker of your language would not use the question form for that purpose, you could translate this as a statement or as an exclamation. Alternate translation: [so they have no wisdom at all!]

10.q: לָ⁠כֵן֩ אֶתֵּ֨ן אֶת נְשֵׁי⁠הֶ֜ם לַ⁠אֲחֵרִ֗ים שְׂדֽוֹתֵי⁠הֶם֙ לְ⁠י֣וֹרְשִׁ֔ים כִּ֤י מִ⁠קָּטֹן֙ וְ⁠עַד גָּד֔וֹל כֻּלֹּ֖⁠ה בֹּצֵ֣עַ בָּ֑צַע מִ⁠נָּבִיא֙ וְ⁠עַד כֹּהֵ֔ן כֻּלֹּ֖⁠ה עֹ֥שֶׂה שָּֽׁקֶר
10.note: If it would be more natural in your language, you could reverse the order of these phrases, since the second phrase gives the reason for the result that the first phrase describes. Alternate translation: [Because from the least to the greatest, everyone is greedy for dishonest gain, and from the prophet to the priest, everyone deals deceitfully, therefore I will give their wives to others, their fields to those possessing them]

Yahweh is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [and their fields I will give to those possessing them]

Yahweh is referring to all of the people by naming two extremes, **the least** and **the greatest**. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [from the most unimportant to the most important people]

Yahweh is referring to all of the religious leaders by naming two major components, **the prophet** and **the priest**. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [Among all the religious leaders]

11.q: וַ⁠יְרַפּ֞וּ אֶת שֶׁ֤בֶר בַּת עַמִּ⁠י֙ עַל נְקַלָּ֔ה
11.note: Yahweh is speaking as if the ruin of his people were a wound and as if the prophets and priests were treating that wound carelessly, since he says that they have **healed the brokenness** of his people **lightly**. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [For they have dealt superficially with the ruin of my people]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **brokenness**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [the broken daughter of my people]

Yahweh is using **the daughter of my people** as a common expression of the culture to mean “my dear people.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [my dear people]

The prophets and priests are repeating the word **Peace** in order to intensify their expression of the idea that it conveys. If your language can repeat words for intensification, it would be appropriate to do that here in your translation. If not, your language may have another way of expressing the intensification. Alternate translation: [There will be complete peace]

12.note: Yahweh is using the question form to assert that these people felt no shame at all for the detestable things they did. If a speaker of your language would not use the question form for that purpose, you could translate this as a statement or as an exclamation. Alternate translation: [They should have been ashamed when they did an abomination!]

Yahweh is repeating forms of the verb **ashamed** in order to intensify his expression of the idea that it conveys. If your language can repeat words for intensification, it would be appropriate to do that here in your translation. If not, your language may have another way of expressing the intensification. Alternate translation: [they were not ashamed at all]

The expression **to be humiliated** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [they did not know how to feel ashamed]
Here, **fall** represents die. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [they will die]

Yahweh is using the adjective **fallen** as a noun to mean a certain kind of person. Your language may use adjectives in the same way. If not, you can translate this adjective with an equivalent phrase. Alternate translation: [those who have already fallen]

Jeremiah is repeating forms of the verb **fall** in order to intensify his expression of the idea that it conveys. If your language can repeat words for intensification, it would be appropriate to do that here in your translation. If not, your language may have another way of expressing the intensification. Alternate translation: [they will certainly die, along with everyone else who dies]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **punishment**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [at the time when I punish them]

13.note: Yahweh is repeating forms of the verb **gather** in order to intensify his expression of the idea that it conveys. If your language can repeat words for intensification, it would be appropriate to do that here in your translation. If not, your language may have another way of expressing the intensification. Alternate translation: [I will completely gather them]

13.q: אֵין֩ עֲנָבִ֨ים בַּ⁠גֶּ֜פֶן וְ⁠אֵ֧ין תְּאֵנִ֣ים בַּ⁠תְּאֵנָ֗ה וְ⁠הֶֽ⁠עָלֶה֙ נָבֵ֔ל
13.note: Yahweh is speaking as if his people were a **vine** and a **fig tree** that bear no fruit and whose leaves have dried up. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [my people produce nothing good at all, and they are dying]

The pronoun **they** refers to the grapes, figs, and leaves that Yahweh gave to his people, while the pronoun **them** refers to the people of Judah. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [those things have disappeared from the people]

14.note: The people are using the question form to urge one another to act rather than to ask for information. If a speaker of your language would not use the question form for that purpose, you could translate this as a statement or as an exclamation. Alternate translation: [We should not remain sitting here!]
This is the beginning of what the people of Judah said. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could mark that this is a direct quote of the people.

The expression **Be gathered** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [Let us gather together]

The people are speaking as if the judgment that Yahweh has brought on them were **water of poison** that he made them drink. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and has brought deadly judgment upon us]

15.q: קַוֵּ֥ה לְ⁠שָׁל֖וֹם וְ⁠אֵ֣ין ט֑וֹב לְ⁠עֵ֥ת מַרְפֵּ֖ה וְ⁠הִנֵּ֥ה בְעָתָֽה
15.note: These two clauses mean basically the same thing. The second emphasizes the meaning of the first by repeating the same idea with different words. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could combine them and express the emphasis in another way. Alternate translation: [We were confidently expecting well-being, but instead we experienced only utter disaster]

The people are leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [and we were hoping for a time of healing, but behold, terror came]

Jeremiah is using the term **behold** to focus his listeners’ attention on what he is about to say. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation. Alternate translation: [look, terror came instead]

16.note: The pronoun **his** refers to the enemy who is coming to attack Judah, whom Yahweh has not yet named. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [The snorting of the enemy’s horses]

The expression **was heard** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [rings out]

The implication is that **Dan** lay at the northern edge of the land, so the sound of the approaching army could already be heard at the border. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [from Dan, at the northern border of the land]

Yahweh is speaking as if the enemy’s war horses were **mighty ones**, that is, powerful warriors. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [the neighing of his powerful stallions]

Yahweh says that **the whole land quakes** as an extreme statement for emphasis. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use a different way to express the emphasis. Alternate translation: [the land seems to tremble everywhere]

The word translated as **for** indicates that what follows is a reason for what came before. Use a connector in your language that makes it clear that what follows is a reason for what came before. Alternate translation: [because they have come]

Yahweh is speaking as if the invading army were a creature devouring its food, since he says that they have **consumed the land**. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and destroyed the land and everything in it]

17.q: הִנְ⁠נִ֨י מְשַׁלֵּ֜חַ בָּ⁠כֶ֗ם נְחָשִׁים֙ צִפְעֹנִ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר אֵין לָ⁠הֶ֖ם לָ֑חַשׁ
17.note: Yahweh is speaking as if the enemies he is sending against his people were **snakes** and **vipers** that no one can control. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [behold, I am sending enemies among you who are like snakes, like vipers that no one can charm]

Yahweh is using **behold me sending snakes among you** as a common expression of the culture to mean that he is about to do something. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [Now I am about to send snakes among you]

The implication is that people of this culture believed that snakes could be controlled by charming them, but no one will be able to control these snakes in that way. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [that no one will be able to control by charming them]

18.note: This is the beginning of what Jeremiah said. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could mark that this is a direct quote of Jeremiah. See the UST.

Jeremiah is using **Joy of me in sorrow** as a common expression of the culture to mean that his gladness has failed under his grief. If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [My gladness has given way to grief]

Jeremiah is speaking as if his **heart** were **faint**, that is, weak and sick, in order to describe how deeply he grieves. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [I feel utterly weak deep inside]

19.q: הַֽ⁠יהוָה֙ אֵ֣ין בְּ⁠צִיּ֔וֹן אִם מַלְכָּ֖⁠הּ אֵ֣ין בָּ֑⁠הּ
19.note: The people are using the question form to express their despair that Yahweh has abandoned them. If a speaker of your language would not use the question form for that purpose, you could translate this as a statement or as an exclamation. Alternate translation: [Yahweh is no longer in Zion! Her king is no longer in her!]

The implication is that **her king** is Yahweh, who reigns over Zion. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [Is Yahweh, her king, no longer in her]
This is the beginning of what Yahweh said in reply. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could mark that this is a direct quote of Yahweh.

Yahweh is using the question form to rebuke his people for worshiping idols. If a speaker of your language would not use the question form for that purpose, you could translate this as a statement or as an exclamation. Alternate translation: [They have provoked me to anger with their idols, with vain foreign things!]

20.q: עָבַ֥ר קָצִ֖יר כָּ֣לָה קָ֑יִץ וַ⁠אֲנַ֖חְנוּ ל֥וֹא נוֹשָֽׁעְנוּ
20.note: The implication is that the seasons in which the people expected help to come have now gone by, and no help has come. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [The harvest has passed and summer has ended, but throughout all that time no one came to help us, and we have not been delivered]

The expression **we have not been delivered** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [and no one has rescued us]

21.note: Jeremiah is repeating forms of the verb **broken** in order to intensify his expression of the idea that it conveys. If your language can repeat words for intensification, it would be appropriate to do that here in your translation. If not, your language may have another way of expressing the intensification. Alternate translation: [Because my people are completely broken, I too am completely broken]

Jeremiah is speaking as if the disaster that has come upon his people and his own grief over it were something that has shattered him into pieces. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [For the destruction of my people I am devastated]

The expression **I am broken** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [my heart breaks]

Jeremiah is speaking of **horror** as if it were a living thing that could take hold of him. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [I am utterly horrified]

22.q: הַ⁠צֳרִי֙ אֵ֣ין בְּ⁠גִלְעָ֔ד אִם רֹפֵ֖א אֵ֣ין שָׁ֑ם
22.note: Jeremiah is using the question form to affirm that there is indeed balm in Gilead and that there are healers there. If a speaker of your language would not use the question form for that purpose, you could translate this as a statement or as an exclamation. Alternate translation: [There is surely balm medicine in Gilead! There is surely a healer there!]

A **medicinal balm** is a kind of sweet-smelling resin that comes from a tree and that people in this culture used as a medicine to soothe and heal wounds. If your readers would not be familiar with what such a balm is, you could use the name of a similar thing that your readers would recognize, or you could use a more general term. Alternate translation: [Is there no healing ointment]

22.q: כִּ֗י מַדּ֨וּעַ֙ לֹ֣א עָֽלְתָ֔ה אֲרֻכַ֖ת בַּת עַמִּֽ⁠י
22.note: Jeremiah is using the question form to lament that his people have not recovered even though the means of healing should be available. If a speaker of your language would not use the question form for that purpose, you could translate this as a statement or as an exclamation. Alternate translation: [Yet the healing of the daughter of my people has not come!]

Jeremiah is speaking as if the restoration of his people were the **healing** of a sick or wounded person. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [the well-being of my dear people]
